title: adaptive-slot-reservation-coordinator-for-continuous-batcher
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds an adaptive slot reservation coordinator to the continuous batcher to reduce KV-pin starvation and improve fairness across latency-sensitive and throughput-sensitive workloads. No API surface changes.
description: Summary: Implement an adaptive slot reservation coordinator for the continuous batching scheduler to address observed starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests when KV-heavy long sequences dominate the batcher. Motivation: Recent production traces and perf canaries showed tail-latency regressions for short-chat requests during KV-intensive traffic bursts. Existing fairness gating was coarse-grained and could not account for KV pin density or request age. This PR introduces a lightweight coordinator that reserves and dynamically reassigns 'execution slots' inside the batcher pool based on multi-factor scoring (request_age, kv_pin_density, estimated_token_cost, and priority_tier). The design favors low-latency requests without creating hard capacity islands and supports graceful soft-preemption when long-running batches exceed soft timeouts. What changed (commits): 1) c1a4d9b initial coordinator implementation: scheduler/slot_coordinator.{cc,h}, continuous_batcher_adaptor.{cc} hooks, metrics and config knobs. 2) 2f9b55e performance fixes: reduce atomic contention, use per-worker minibuckets, optimize kernel selection hints to avoid repeated lookups. 3) 8e7d120 tests and docs: end-to-end unit/integration tests, benchmarking harness script, docs/operations/slot-coordinator.md. Motivation and design highlights: - Adaptive scoring: each queued request exposes metadata (kv_pin_estimate, sequence_len_estimate, arrival_ts, customer_tier). Coordinator computes a score that biases selection towards low-age/low-kv requests when tail latency SLOs are at risk, otherwise relaxes toward throughput maximization. - Soft reservation with decay: slots are soft-reserved for latency-sensitive classes but decay over time (configurable half-life) to prevent permanent partitioning. - Soft preemption: if a running batch exceeds the soft_timeout threshold and there are pending high-priority small requests, the coordinator flags the running batch for early flush (flush of partial tokens + safe KV cache preservation) and reclaims one slot. This uses cooperative preemption to avoid evicting KV pins unsafely. - KV-awareness: the coordinator reads kv_pin_density metrics from the per-request admission token and reduces scheduling preference for requests that would pin a large fraction of K/V cache until a cooldown is observed. - Low overhead: implemented with lock-free rings and per-worker minibuckets; adds amortized ~0.5% CPU on steady state in microbenchmarks. Files changed (high-level): - runtime/scheduler/slot_coordinator.cc/h - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher_adaptor.cc - runtime/kv_cache/kv_pin_metrics.cc/h - runtime/config/slot_coordinator_config.yaml - tests/scheduler/slot_coordinator_unit_test.cc - tests/integration/slot_coordinator_e2e.sh - docs/operations/slot-coordinator.md - bench/perf/slot-coordinator-bench.py - examples/slot-coordinator-configs/local.yaml - CI: .github/workflows/slot-coordinator.yml (adds targeted perf jobs) Testing and results: - Unit tests: new coverage for scoring logic and decay semantics. - Integration: stress runs with mixed workloads show 35-60% reduction in P95 latency for short requests under KV-heavy background load, with <3% throughput regression on long sequence workloads. - Canary perf runs on staging TV showed stable KV cache hit ratios and reduced tail spikes. CI and review timeline: - Initial CI run: failed one flaky test: tests/integration/heavy_kv_emulation (timeout). - Rerun CI after adding a small test timeout increase and improved test harness determinism; subsequent run passed full matrix. Review comments and responses (excerpted): - Thomas: "Can we avoid adding global coordinator state that serializes admission?" Author: "Coordinator is sharded per worker with a light aggregation layer; code and comments updated to clarify no central lock is used." - Elena: "What guarantees do we have for KV cache consistency if we preempt a batch?" Author: "Added a safe-eviction path: we preserve KV pins for partial sequences and attach a reclamation token; documented in runtime/kv_cache/README and tested in e2e." - Marco: "Add observability: per-slot occupancy and preemption counters." Author: "Added metrics: scheduler.slot_reserved_count, scheduler.slot_preemptions_total, scheduler.score_distribution{quantiles}." - QA: "Repro scenario for flaky test included; added histogram seeding to reduce nondeterminism." Merge and rollout plan: - PR merged via squash on 2026-02-22 after approvals from Thomas and Elena. - Feature gated behind runtime.feature_slots_v1 toggle; rollout plan: enable in Canary region for 48 hours, monitor P95/P99, KV hit ratio, and per-slot preemption counters; then progressively roll to production. Backwards compatibility and impact: - No changes to public API. - Configurable toggle and knobs allow safe rollback. - Documentation added under docs/operations with tuning recommendations and suggested knobs for tenants with heavy KV workloads. Notes for on-call: - Alert to create: Increase in scheduler.slot_preemptions_total without corresponding decrease in scheduler.latency_p95 suggests coordinator is not effective and should be disabled. - If unexpected KV cache churn appears, disable feature toggle and consult runtime/kv_cache owner. Related work and references: - ENG-3842 design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3842/slot-reservation-coordinator-design - Related PRs: follow-up will integrate prioritized batching with dedicated GPU pools (planned ENG-3999). Why this is unique: Instead of simple age-based or token-bucket heuristics this PR combines KV-awareness, decaying soft reservations, and cooperative soft-preemption to reduce starvation without hard partitioning. It also emphasizes low overhead and safe KV cache semantics.
